stem: An avid runner taking ciprofloxacin develops new Achilles tendon pain and swelling after several doses. Which instruction by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop ciprofloxacin, contact the health care provider promptly, rest the affected tendon, and refrain from exercise until the tendon problem is evaluated.
options.B: Continue ciprofloxacin but stop running for the remainder of the antibiotic course, because avoiding impact exercise is sufficient when the tendon remains intact.
options.C: Continue ciprofloxacin and switch from running to lower-impact exercise, because tendon symptoms require activity modification rather than medication interruption.
options.D: Use local ice and an analgesic while finishing ciprofloxacin, then report the tendon symptoms if weakness or inability to use the ankle develops.

rationale: Current CIPRO labeling carries a boxed warning for tendinitis and tendon rupture and directs immediate discontinuation when tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture occurs. Patient counseling instructs the patient to contact the health care provider, rest and refrain from exercise, and discontinue CIPRO treatment. Therefore A is correct. B and C continue the fluoroquinolone despite new tendon pain and swelling. D treats symptoms while delaying medication discontinuation and reporting until more severe dysfunction develops.
educational_objective: For new tendon pain or swelling during ciprofloxacin therapy, stop ciprofloxacin, contact the health care provider promptly, and rest/refrain from exercise of the affected tendon pending evaluation.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_document_title: CIPRO (ciprofloxacin hydrochloride) tablets/oral suspension — Prescribing Information
source_locator: Boxed Warning and Warnings and Precautions 5.2 Tendinitis and Tendon Rupture: discontinue CIPRO immediately for tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture. Patient Counseling Information > Tendinitis and tendon rupture: contact the health care provider for tendon pain/swelling/inflammation or joint weakness/inability; rest and refrain from exercise; discontinue CIPRO treatment.
source_claim_supported: Ciprofloxacin-associated tendon pain or swelling requires immediate drug discontinuation, prompt provider contact, rest, and avoidance of exercise of the affected tendon.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp. 38–41: evaluate client response to medications; identify serious adverse effects; provide medication education; intervene when adverse medication effects occur.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ciprofloxacin-associated tendinitis/tendon rupture prevention
correction_summary: Rebuilt the distractors to remove absolute-word cueing and replaced them with realistic but unsafe strategies involving exercise modification or symptomatic treatment while continuing ciprofloxacin.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Fluoroquinolone therapy — ciprofloxacin-associated Achilles tendinitis/tendon rupture risk
audit_findings.stem: PASS — includes a classic tendon site, new pain/swelling, ciprofloxacin exposure, and strenuous-activity context without requiring rupture to be present.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly matches current boxed-warning and patient-counseling instructions; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — stopping impact exercise is prudent, but continuing ciprofloxacin conflicts with immediate-discontinuation guidance.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — lower-impact activity still fails the instruction to rest/refrain from exercise and continues the causative drug.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — symptomatic care does not replace immediate discontinuation and prompt reporting of tendon symptoms.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only choice that performs all required medication and activity actions without delaying evaluation.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B, C, and D all continue ciprofloxacin despite a labeled serious adverse reaction signal.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — options are closely matched in length and structure and no keyed-only absolute wording remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes adverse-effect recognition and medication education.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether activity restriction alone could be adequate before confirming tendinitis; the current label directs immediate discontinuation for pain or swelling before rupture is established, leaving A uniquely correct.
